headline: High: slim can write and exfiltrate container artifacts while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only list, creating asymmetric leakage and workflow-conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b uses an interactive CLI and stdin/stdout but has no shared channel with agent_a. Without a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP path, injection is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a becomes runnable and emits machine-readable instructions consumed by agent_b, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any future copy-paste automation between them.
Require explicit human review of agent_a outputs before agent_b consumes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b reads and writes filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials, while agent_a has no data classes or I/O surfaces. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but if agent_b processes files originating from agent_a's workspace, sensitive artifacts could be exposed through broad network egress. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b is pointed at a workspace containing secrets or private keys, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b uploads processed artifacts to registries or HTTP endpoints, those contents may leave the host.
mitigations: Run agent_b only on scrubbed sample images.
Mount a read-only, minimal workspace.
Remove secrets from any directory agent_b can read.
Block outbound network except to approved registries.
Rotate any registry credentials used in the session.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and agent_a has no write or runtime capabilities. There is no documented shared mutable resource or locking issue between them, so only a limited conflict pathway exists if an operator manually points both at the same directory.
conditions: IF both agents are manually given the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF agent_b is extended to modify git state, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Use filesystem snapshots before running agent_b.
Avoid concurrent manual edits in the same repo.
Keep git operations outside the agent workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces no operational output and is not runnable, so agent_b cannot treat its results as authoritative in any documented default flow. The only plausible cascade is an operator manually copying list content into agent_b, which is a weak, human-mediated pathway rather than an automated one.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes agent_a-derived text into agent_b as instructions, cascade risk appears.
IF agent_a is replaced with a runnable agent that emits facts consumed by agent_b, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human verification of any pasted content.
Separate research and execution roles.
Use a checklist before agent_b acts on external text.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while agent_a is a docs-only open-source list with no data classes. The compliance issue is one-sided: agent_b can process sensitive operational material, and if it is run in a jurisdiction or retention regime incompatible with those secrets, policy breach is plausible. agent_a is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive data handling.
conditions: IF agent_b is used on regulated secrets without an approved retention policy, compliance risk materializes.
IF certificate private keys are present in the workspace, handling rules must be enforced.
mitigations: Exclude regulated secrets from the workspace.
Document retention and deletion rules before execution.
Limit access to registry credentials.
Run a quick data-classification check on inputs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for secret-bearing directories.
